authority_note: Budgets are guidelines, not enforced. The GM has authority to adapt as play goes (Caleb, 2026-10-04). Anything under 'authoritative' follows a filed source; anything under 'assumed' or tagged ASSUMED is a proposal for Caleb/GM to adjust.

list.what: Tier-to-band map: F1 trivial=half of Low, standard=Low, hard=Moderate, boss=High (matches overview 9.2). F2+ trivial=Low, standard=Moderate, hard=High (elite), boss=High (core 8.3: mostly Moderate, some Low, 1-3 High per floor).

Encounter density: F1 fixed list (6 planned, max 8); F2-F6 1.5 encounters per clock day, no quota; mix = boss 1, hard 15%, trivial 25%, standard rest.

Days: F4=20, F5=25, F6=30 are a HOUSE RULE (room vote, majority of six, 2026-10-04, Q-001 as revised, passed 6 of 6; Caleb can veto or change; GM-adaptable). The canon timers 10/15/17 (M-603..M-608) are reference only (authoritative.clock.days_canon_reference). F7+ is held at 30 for the growth curve (placeholder, ASSUMED: floors do not get shorter than F6, per Caleb's rule that floors get longer as you go down). F1=5, F2=10, F3=20 are authoritative.

Encounter credits per Crawler by tier (F1 scale): trivial 0-2, standard 1d4x2, hard 1d6x2, boss 1d6x5; pool = per-Crawler x party size, split evenly. F1 values are sized so a 4-Crawler party's spot amounts in the overview (about 158 credits across the floor) fit inside the tiers.
R1 toast credits 10-40 (avg 25); expected credit-paying R1 toasts per Crawler: F1 2, F2 3, F3+ 3.

Per-encounter box odds are the fight share of core 4.5 targets; non-fight deed Bronze expected 0.5 (F1) and 0.9 (F2) per Crawler. F1 total Bronze (incl. Welcome) is 1.9 expected, inside the overview's 1-3; F2 about 2.0, the low end of core 2-4.

F2 Boss Box is Silver (core 4.7 cap) and F2 box values equal F1's: the F1 live decks are reused for F2 (no F2 decks exist yet). Welcome Box uses decks z06 + any, fight/deed Bronze boxes use all F1 decks pooled, the Boss Box uses z10 (Boss) + any.
Encounter credits on F5+ takes the credit multiplier (x5); box pulls do not (decision 019).

Rest-without-saferoom fee 20 per Crawler (cap 60 per floor); key bribe 50 per Crawler; Detour Tax 75 per Crawler (a missed Stairwell key ONLY; a missed collapse is death with no toll, decision 026); Zone S forcing fee 25 per Crawler; detour 2 hours, 0 rest slots; collapse steps cost hooks and services, 0 credits.
Safe-room adjacency and rest-segment limits (see adjacency).

Optional safety valve (not required under the per-floor line): before a Floor 2 Boss Box, if the Crawler's running total on that floor is 900 or more, the GM may hand-pick that box from cards worth 175 or less. Run it from `state.py loot totals --include-credits` (the tool change now exists, Q-003).
Reward ladder for the six proposed achievements (floors.1.achievement_rewards).

rest_without_saferoom.long_rest_rule: Long Rest only in saferooms (core 5.6; overview rule 7); a field attempt is interrupted by Ceiling Ticks after 1d4 hours
rest_without_saferoom.reasoning: 20 credits = 40% of one Potion of Healing (50) and below the R1 toast band (10-40); 3 billings cap at 60 = 4% of a floor's 1,500 line. A saferoom is free, so the fee only has to sting, not threaten.

stairwell_key_terminal_bribe.where: Floor 1 Break Room (Z6) Snakk-Matic terminal; gone on Day 4 when the Break Room and vendors lose service (decision 026)
stairwell_key_terminal_bribe.haggle: allowed at the terminal's normal DC 13 / 15% off (core 5.10; overview 5.6), GM may refuse
stairwell_key_terminal_bribe.reasoning: 50 per Crawler = one Potion of Healing each (3.3% of a floor's 1,500 line). It buys the key without the Bruiser fight; using the key to skip the Z10 fight also forfeits the Silver Boss Box (about 482 credits of expected value), so the bribe is cheap in credits and expensive in opportunity.

detour_tax.what: The System's Detour Tax toll. It covers ONLY a missed Stairwell key: a Crawler who reaches the Zone S door without the key may pay it as one of the three costs the day spec lists (detour back to Z8 or Z6, this toll, or the loud keyless forcing). It is NOT a collapse toll: a missed floor collapse is death on every floor, with no toll (decision 026, Caleb ruling ~10:02 PM CT). The collapse steps themselves cost hooks and services only.
detour_tax.does_not_apply_to: a missed floor collapse (death, no toll)
detour_tax.shortfall: a Crawler who cannot pay pays what they have and the GM logs the balance (no debt mechanic)
detour_tax.reasoning: 75 = 1.5 x the bribe (waiting costs more than buying early) and 5% of a floor's 1,500 line. The real cost of a missed key is time, danger or the forfeited Boss Box (about 482 expected credits), not the toll.

zone_s_door_forcing.mechanics_source: overview 5.10: Thieves' Tools DC 15 or Strength (Athletics) DC 15, 10 minutes, loud; Dean Thudd and his Ushers come looking 1 minute later
zone_s_door_forcing.reasoning: 25 per Crawler is the cheapest in credits because forcing already pays in danger (the boss arrives at the Crawlers' worst moment). Ordering: forcing 25 < bribe 50 < Detour Tax 75.

detour.note: Walking back to Z8 or Z6 while they still serve: 2 in-game hours, no rest slot consumed, 4 extra d6 Ceiling Tick rolls (one per 30 minutes, overview rule 6).

collapse_step_costs.model: Each collapse step costs the party the hooks and services in the closed zones (loot, achievements, vendors), not credits; the Detour Tax (missed key only) is the only credit toll on the clock (day spec collapse_order_status). Missing the final collapse is death, not a price. The way to Z9, Z10, Z11 is never cut.

q6_crafting_price_proposal.what_it_replaces: (Adopted in v0.1.6 for Floors 3-18.) The credit multiplier (x1 F1-4, x5 F5-9, x20 F10-14, x50 F15-18, core 3.9) as applied to CRAFTING PRICES ONLY (basic table 5,000 / Crafting Studio 12,000 / Enhanced Studio 30,000 at Floor-1 scale, rules/20). Achievement rewards, encounter credits, R1 toast credits and all other System fees keep the core multiplier.
method: liquid income L(f) = the growth table's liquid_if_items_sold_at_half. Plain note: L halves box ITEMS only (core 5.10); credit-pull cards are NOT halved, they count at full value (credits per Crawler per floor if every box item is sold at half credit_value, core 5.10, plus encounter credits and R1 credits).
trend T(f) = log-linear fit of L over F3-F18 (about x1.348 per floor).

smoothed income S(f) = sqrt(L(f) x T(f)), halfway (geometric) between this floor's income and the trend, so a single tier step (Gold F3, Platinum F9, Legendary F13) or the F15 dip does not swing prices all at once.

proposed price = target x S(f), rounded (500 under 20,000; 1,000 under 100,000; 5,000 under 1,000,000; 10,000 above), and never lower than the previous floor's price. Three hand adjustments from the Accountant's vote (v0.1.7): F8 held at the F7 price, F13 raised, F18 held at the F17 price.
implied_crafting_multiplier = proposed price / Floor-1-scale price; this column is what would replace the credit multiplier for crafting prices.
caveats: Targets are met on average, not floor by floor: income is stepped (box tiers) and prices are smooth, so the ratio is lower right after an income step (F9, F13) and higher right before one (F8, F12) by design.
Income F3-F18 is itself a placeholder (no F3+ decks), so the schedule must be rerun if the growth table changes.
Prices rise with the trend even when F15-F18 income dips (non-decreasing rule), so the F15-18 ratios drift up; that is the cost of keeping prices smooth.
Applied in rules/20 (current section 9.1a; sections 0, 2.5.3, 9.1 and 10 cite this schedule instead of the credit multiplier for the three workstation prices).
